newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand slumped to its worst level of the day towards the close on Monday following the release of far weaker-than-expected August trade figures during the afternoon, dealers said.

Late importer demand put further pressure on the unit which ended at 4.5300/5350 against the dollar, little changed from its Friday close of 4.5320/5370. In after-hours trade, it fell further to 4.5370/5400 on the dollar.
"There was a lot of short-covering on the back of the trade figures," one dealer said.
"The figures were a lot worse than the market expected and took the rand back to its opening levels," he added.

Figures released on Monday showed South Africa's trade account falling to a 132.4 million rand surplus in August from a 2.58 billion rand surplus in July. Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast a surplus of 760 million rand.

Earlier in the day, the rand had touched a best level of 4.5150 bid on exporter demand, dollar sales from offshore and reports that the International Monetary Fund believed the rand's recent depreciation had been overdone.
Dealers said activity had been moderate, picking up towards the close as players digested the trade figures. Some good two-way flows were seen during the day.
"Importers were around at the 4.52 level and when the rand moved to 4.53, dollars were coming in," a dealer said.
Traders said they expected a range of 4.51-4.54 on Tuesday with the unit seen toppish at the 4.53-4.5350 level.
Against the crosses the local unit weakened slightly to last trade at 7.0898/0999 from 7.0888/0988 against sterling late on Friday and at 0.3359/3364 marks from 0.3354/3360 previously.
Bonds weakened in tandem with the rand and on a late reaction to the trade figures, retracing from the firmer levels traded at for most of the day, dealers said.
"People spent the afternoon mulling over the trade surplus figure which was pretty bad. The rand weakening back to 4.53 also took bonds weaker," a dealer said.

At 1400 GMT the key R150 was at 15.12 percent from 15.10 percent late on Friday. In after-hours trade bonds weakened further to touch a worst level of 15.195 following late offshore selling, dealers said.
"We saw some selling out of London, some guys taking profit," a dealer said.
They said players had also held long positions for most of the afternoon and became panicky as yields moved higher.
"When they saw the long bond (R150) kicking up, they got a bit nervous and started to cut their positions," the trader said.
Dealers said they expected bonds to trade in a 15.10-15.20 percent range on Tuesday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners bought a net 120.35 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling a net 44.65 million rand the previous day.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 3.42 billion rand on Friday from 37.95 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.70 to 15.90 percent, while 90-day BAs were unchanged at 15.15 to 15.30 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage slightly lower at 7.853 billion rand on Saturday from 7.886 billion on Friday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
